risk_if_not_implemented: Without Unique System-Generated Session Identifiers, credentials may be phished, replayed, guessed or stolen, allowing unauthorized actors to authenticate as trusted identities. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unauthorized Access (R-AC-4), Identity Compromise / Impersonation (R-AC-5), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Technical / Mechanical Failure (MT-10).

compensating_control_1.name: Integrity of Data In Transit
compensating_control_1.description: Cryptographic mechanisms exist to detect unauthorized changes to data in transit.
compensating_control_1.justification: Integrity of Data In Transit (CRY-06) provides cryptographic protection that compensates for the absence of Unique System-Generated Session Identifiers (IAC-47) by ensuring data confidentiality and integrity through alternative technical means. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Session Integrity
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to protect the authenticity and integrity of communications sessions.
compensating_control_2.justification: Session Integrity (NET-29) provides cryptographic protection that compensates for the absence of Unique System-Generated Session Identifiers (IAC-47) by ensuring data confidentiality and integrity through alternative technical means. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
